target.title: fix(agents): strip runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105113: runtime stream-boundary markers (`[e~[` / `[e[`) leak as a trailing suffix in user-visible channel deliveries (reported on Telegram with MiniMax/MiniMax-M3).

## Root Cause

`sanitizeUserFacingText` strips `<tool_call>`, `<function_calls>`, `<system-reminder>`, and other scaffolding, but does not cover `[e~[` — a runtime stream-boundary marker functionally analogous to SSE `[DONE]`.

## Fix

Add `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` to the `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline. Per ClawSweeper review, the regexes are **narrowed to trailing-suffix only**:

- `[e~[` / `[e[` — only stripped at the **end of text** (trailing suffix), not globally. Inline references like `"[e~[ is a stream marker"` are preserved.
- Trailing lone `[` after whitespace — truncated marker fragment
- `[1]` — **removed entirely** (even trailing can be a legitimate citation)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` | `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` — narrowed to suffix-only |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts` | Updated tests: suffix stripping + inline preservation |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — narrowed to trailing suffix only

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { sanitizeUserFacingText } from '...'"

Trailing suffix stripped:
  "Hello, how can I help?[e~["     → "Hello, how can I help?"   ✅
  "The answer is 42.[e~["          → "The answer is 42."        ✅
  "[e~["                           → ""                         ✅

Inline references preserved:
  "[e~[ is a stream marker"        → unchanged                  ✅
  "The marker [e~[ appears here"   → unchanged                  ✅

Bracket citations preserved:
  "See [1] and [2] for details"    → unchanged                  ✅
  "RFC [1] defines the protocol"   → unchanged                  ✅
```

### Vitest

```
✓ strips trailing runtime stream-boundary markers (#105113)
✓ preserves inline [e~[ references that are not trailing markers
✓ preserves all inline bracket references
✓ removes trailing lone bracket fragments
```
